title: Non-interventional, prospective health services research study on the course of testosterone levels during androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with LHRH analogues (3-month depot).
summary:
Prostate carcinoma is the most common male tumor in Germany, with approximately 65,000 new cases per year (Robert Koch Institute, 2017). In advanced prostate cancer, androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) is a frequently used form of therapy. The therapeutic goal of ADT in this context is the suppression of testosterone levels. Currently, however, there is little systematically collected data on the effectiveness of the various drugs used.
In the therapy of advanced, hormonal prostate carcinoma, drug-based ADT using appropriate drugs (LHRH analogues) has always played a decisive role. The therapeutic goal is to lower the testosterone level, which leads to an inhibition of the growth of prostate cancer cells and thus enables an effective therapy of the disease at this stage. The guideline for prostate cancer therapy currently recommends lowering testosterone levels on ADT to less than 20-50 ng/dl. However, recent study data indicate that lowering testosterone below 20 ng/dl may result in improved overall survival.
Against this background, d-uo is initiating a non-interventional health care research study on the course of ADT using LHRH analogues to investigate to what extent these guideline recommendations are realized in the everyday care of German uro-oncology and which testosterone levels are achieved under continuous ADT.
Furthermore, the use of ADT in Germany will be investigated descriptively. The respective therapies will be investigated with regard to the occurrence of side effects, the disease-specific quality of life of the treated patients and the medical outcome. The study was designed accordingly as an observational study; the observation period of the treated patients is one year.

interventions.name: Over a period of one year, the testosterone values, PSA values and other existing parameters relating to the type of therapy and the course of the disease are documented on a quarterly basis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. age >= 18 years
2. written informed consent and consent for the processing of personal data are available.
3. patients with advanced hormonal prostate carcinoma, in whom the indication for ADT exists and a corresponding drug treatment is planned independently of the participation in this study.
Exclusion criteria:
1. bilateral orchiectomy
2. hypersensitivity to LHRH analogues according to the respective technical information
3. previous hormone therapy
